kernelIdea: Conjecture a general formula from the first few cases by spotting several patterns at once, then prove it by induction, handling the base case carefully.

kernels.l1: Double it, then double it again. The pattern keeps going.
kernels.l2: If you keep doing the same step over and over, a pattern appears. Guess the pattern, then use the domino idea to be sure it never breaks.
kernels.l3: Compute the first few cases of a repeated process, look for a formula covering all of them, then prove the formula by the domino argument. Guessing and proving are two different jobs.
kernels.l4: Repeated application of a step produces data; conjecture a closed formula by spotting each pattern separately, then prove it by induction. The base case is the zeroth application, which is the original object.
kernels.l5: Conjecture-then-prove is the working mathematician’s loop: compute cases, isolate each pattern, assemble a formula, prove by induction.
kernels.l6: The nth derivative of 1/x follows this pattern: sign, factorial, and exponent are three separate patterns assembled into one formula and proved by induction.
kernels.l7: For f(x) = 1/x, f^{(n)}(x) = (−1)ⁿ n! x^{−(n+1)}, conjectured by isolating three patterns in the first few derivatives and proved by induction using (k+1)! = (k+1)·k!.
kernels.l8: Induction on the order of differentiation is the standard route to Leibniz’s rule, Taylor coefficients, and closed forms for higher derivatives generally.

objectives: Conjecture a general formula from data
